questions.q: What question does the baseline doc answer that the runbook doesn't?
options: What do we do when something happens
What does our environment actually look like right now
Who is on call this week
How much does Sentinel ingestion cost
questions.explain: The runbook answers procedure; the baseline doc answers current state.

questions.q: What are the four sections of the baseline doc?
options: Budget, timeline, stakeholders, sign-off
Ingestion, identity, network, response
Detection, triage, remediation, validation
Windows, Linux, firewall, cloud
questions.explain: The doc covers ingestion sources, the CA pilot, the corrected firewall rule, and a pointer to the runbook, organized under those four headings.

questions.q: Where does the incident's worked example live, and why not in the baseline doc too?
options: It lives in the runbook, because the baseline doc is a current-state snapshot, not an incident history
It lives only in the baseline doc, since the runbook is procedure-only
It is not documented anywhere
It lives in both documents in full detail
questions.explain: Duplicating incident history into the baseline doc would turn it into a second incident report instead of a clean snapshot.

questions.q: What is the real distinction between a baseline doc and a runbook?
options: There is no real distinction -- they are interchangeable
A baseline doc describes current state (a snapshot); a runbook describes what to do when something happens (a procedure)
A baseline doc is only for compliance audits
A runbook is only used before an incident, never during one
questions.explain: Snapshot versus procedure is the functional distinction the lesson draws between the two documents.

questions.q: What test does Mara use while writing the baseline doc?
options: Whether Renee has already read it
Whether a new hire who's never seen the environment could understand it in five minutes without asking her directly
Whether it is at least 20 pages long
Whether it includes every log line from the incident
questions.explain: That readability-cold standard is what keeps the doc short and current-state-only.
